q: Parity decision trees and their connection to Fourier analysis: the XOR lemma (Yao, Blum-Luby-Rubinfeld) states that for a function f which is hard on average for small circuits:
opts: f^⊕n (the XOR of n copies) is easier
f^⊕n = f(x₁) ⊕ ... ⊕ f(xₙ) is exponentially harder — hardness amplification
The XOR of n copies is always hard for n ≥ 2
exp: XOR lemma (direct product / hardness amplification): if f is δ-hard (best circuit succeeds with probability ≤ 1/2 + δ), then f^⊕n (XOR of n copies on separate inputs) is 2^{-Ω(n)}-hard. This amplifies weak hardness to strong hardness. The proof uses the Fourier representation of Boolean functions on the hypercube.
